Subject: Re: sudden latency spikes during long-context runs

Hi Irene / team,

We're seeing sustained p99 regressions on the hosted API starting ~2026-11-10T18:45Z. Baseline p99 for our workload (16k/32k contexts) is ~800ms; over the last 90 minutes it's spiked to ~4.2s with an increase in 502/timeout responses. Sample request IDs attached in perf_snapshot_1110.txt.

Impact: our end users experience stalled generation during long-context queries (search + summarization pipeline). This is blocking a time-sensitive rollout — if this continues we'll have to pause traffic.

What we've observed:
- Increased tail latency correlates with bursts of multi-turn 32k requests (user sessions send several concatenated documents).
- Error rate rises during the same windows; p95 also shifted from 300ms -> ~1.1s.
- No config changes on our side.

We need an ETA for mitigation and whether you can temporarily throttle or route us to a workaround (smaller window / model variant / priority lane). Happy to jump on a call.

Selena
CTO, Nova Labs

Subject: Re: sudden latency spikes during long-context runs — initial triage

Marissa — quick findings from initial telemetry:
- Scope: spikes are visible across a subset of hosted clusters in us-west-2; correlated with a 3x increase in high-context (>=16k) request volume starting 18:40Z.
- Symptoms: p95 rose ~2.5x, p99 ~5x. We also see elevated connection queue depths and KV cache miss rates for prefix caching on the shared pool.
- Errors: majority are 502/504 from frontend timeouts when backend batch assembly exceeds 3s.

Immediate mitigations we propose (can be applied within 15–30m):
1) Enable tenant-level fallback routing: route Nova Labs' >16k requests to a smaller-context-compatible model variant that has guarded batching.
2) Soft-rate-limit long-context requests to 60% of current sustained peak per-minute volume (transparent to customer).
3) Bump their priority weight on the autoscaler for next 2 hours (temporary capacity credit).

I've attached rprof_1110.json and svc_topology.png to surface the queue hot spots. Please confirm who will action (infra/ops).

—Ben
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
